findings.title: eating as exploitation

The phrase recurs in the Surah 5 cluster around 5:42, 5:62, and 5:63, where corrupt listening, consuming, and failure to restrain are held around the same illicit practice.

findings.title: concealment becomes material erasure
findings.claim: {{ar:ٱلسُّحْتَ}} ({{tr:al-suḥt}}) fixes the object of {{ar:أَكْلِهِمُ}} ({{tr:aklihim}}) as a definite class of destructive forbidden gain. The root imagery of scraping bare, uprooting, and destroying makes the consumed gain itself corrosive. Its rarity matters: the noun is concentrated in 5:42, 5:62, and 5:63, with a destruction-root echo at 20:61, so the final concrete charge is locally load-bearing before the verdict generalizes it. Variant vocalizations change the word's recitational weight without changing the destructive-gain sense, and the term externalizes the concealed failure of 5:61 as a material economy of erasure.

findings.title: formal dispraise construction
findings.claim: {{ar:بِئْسَ}} ({{tr:biʾsa}}) is the formal verb of dispraise, strengthened by the preceding emphatic particle and completed by the following {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) clause. Its severity root colors the verdict as wretched and weighty, while the fixed construction keeps the local function as condemnation. The same formula clusters in Surah 5, including 5:63, 5:79, and 5:80, and here it gathers the tripartite list into an evaluative landing. The hamza catch is a sound pressure point: the smoothed variant eases the pronunciation without changing the verdict.

findings.title: adjacent verdict frame

findings.title: habitual concealment to habitual doing
findings.claim: {{ar:كَانُوا۟}} ({{tr:kānū}}) frames the final imperfect as habitual past practice. It does not add a separate act; it makes the doing a persisted state belonging to the same plural group carried through the ayah. As part of a familiar condemnation pattern, the auxiliary lets the dispraise judge persisted conduct rather than a momentary act. It also links the boundary from habitual concealment in 5:61 to habitual doing in 5:62, holding the clause open until the final action word arrives.

findings.title: moving scene of many
findings.claim: {{ar:يُسَٰرِعُونَ}} ({{tr:yusāriʿūna}}) shows the many in motion while they are being seen. Because it is completed by {{ar:فِى}} ({{tr:fī}}) rather than a simple goal marker, the racing takes place inside the field that follows. Form III adds a competitive or reciprocal pressure: they are not merely quick but vying in culpable movement. Surah 5 uses this rushing motif in 5:41, 5:52, and 5:62, while positive racing scenes such as 3:114 and 21:90 show that urgency itself is redirected here toward the wrong field. The long medial beat of the form also lets the rushing occupy audible space before landing in the condemned domain, carrying the prior hidden posture into public momentum.
